name: ástvinr
idol: Howard Hill, "He Who Splits the Arrow"
md:
*Beloved Friend.* **Holder:** Puhihwikwasu'u. **Idol:** Howard Hill, "He Who Splits the Arrow". **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** Howard Hill hunted with a close circle, and the story they told is that he loosed arrows only to cover the one standing beside him.

**Blueprint, Bond Shot (at will).** At dawn name one ally as your beloved. When an attack targets your beloved within 120 feet and you can see them, you may use your reaction to loose an arrow at the attacker; on a hit the attack is turned aside and the attacker takes the arrow's damage. **Parts.** *Warm Fletching:* your beloved has advantage on death saves. *Long Memory:* any arrow of yours your beloved touches returns to your quiver. **Maxim, Every Friend (long rest, 1 minute).** Everyone you call friend within 30 feet counts as your beloved. **Signature Part, Never Alone.** You and your beloved always know each other's direction and distance. **Price.** Each time Bond Shot turns an attack aside, you take half the damage that attack would have dealt.

name: Eplaskot
md:
*Apple-Shot.* **Holder:** Elspeth Nicblar. **Idol:** William Tell, "The Apple Shot." **Burden** 5, **level** 11.

**Story.** A tyrant ordered a father to shoot an apple from his own child's head. The tale insists the arrow could not have touched the child, because the father had already decided it would not.

**Blueprint, Name the Harmless (at will).** Before you loose an arrow, name any creature or object within 60 feet of the target; the arrow cannot harm it, bends around it, and still strikes the target as if it were unobstructed. **Parts.** *Steady Hand:* a creature you have named as harmless cannot be forced to move by your arrows' impact. *The Second Bolt:* a held-back arrow in your quiver strikes anyone who harms the creature you last named, no action required. **Maxim, Tyrant's Wager (long rest, 1 minute).** Choose a creature; every arrow you loose at it is a guaranteed hit, but you must also name a harmless target for each. **Signature Part, The Second Bolt Is Yours.** If you are brought to 0 hit points while holding the Fable, the held-back arrow fires at your killer first. **Price.** You say aloud who you will not hit. If you break that word, the Fable sleeps until dawn.

name: óendanǫr
idol: Howard Hill, "He Who Splits the Arrow"
md:
*The Infinity Arrow.* **Holder:** Paul Humphries. **Idol:** Howard Hill, "He Who Splits the Arrow". **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** Audiences swore Howard Hill always had one more arrow in the air than any man could have loosed.

**Blueprint, Halfway (at will).** Loose an arrow; it stops in the air at the midpoint of its path and hangs there. You may release it as a bonus action, and when it resumes it ignores half cover and three-quarters cover. **Parts.** *Endless Quiver:* you never run out of arrows. *Dichotomy:* an arrow hung in the air for a full round deals an extra die of damage when released. **Maxim, Never Arrives (long rest, 1 minute).** Arrows you have hung cannot be intercepted, destroyed, or deflected.

name: Ýviðarveggr
idol: Dafydd Gam, "The Lame Captain of Agincourt."
md:
*Yew Wall.* **Holder:** Cai Pritchard. **Idol:** Dafydd Gam, "The Lame Captain of Agincourt." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A scout told his king that the French were so many they could not be counted, and Dafydd replied that there were enough to kill, enough to capture, and enough to run away. The line became a rallying cry for the longbow.

**Blueprint, Wall of Shafts (action, short rest).** Loose a volley that plants a 30-foot line of upright arrows. The line is difficult terrain for enemies, and allies behind it have half cover. **Parts.** *Enough to Run:* enemies that end their turn in the line have their speed halved until your next turn. *Brother's Wall:* the wall also counts as cover for any Pritchard behind it. **Maxim, Ten Thousand Yews (long rest, 1 minute).** The wall becomes a 60-foot semicircle and blocks sight and ranged weapons for the other side.

name: Bræðraskot
md:
*Brother-Shot.* **Holder:** Ellis Pritchard. **Idol:** Dafydd Gam. **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** The same Agincourt tale says no Welsh archer ever loosed alone; each shot was answered by his neighbor.

**Blueprint, Answered Shot (reaction, at will).** When an ally within 60 feet hits with a ranged attack, you may loose an arrow at the same target as a reaction. **Parts.** *By the Same Hand:* if the ally is also a Pritchard, the answering arrow deals an extra die of damage. *Two Strings:* the arrow counts as a reaction even if you already used one this round (once per turn). **Maxim, Four Brothers (long rest, 1 minute).** Any ally can trigger Answered Shot, not only allies within 60 feet who hit.

name: Ýviðrmerki
md:
*Yew-Mark.* **Holder:** Rhys Pritchard. **Idol:** Dafydd Gam. **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** Soldiers carried a hanging mark, a splinter of yew, to show the archers where the worst fighting was.

**Blueprint, Mark the Worst (bonus action, at will).** Mark a creature you can see; your allies' ranged attacks against it gain +1d4 to hit, and you always know where it is. **Parts.** *Splinter:* the mark lingers on a creature after it leaves your sight. *Bright Yew:* the mark glows only to allies. **Maxim, Ten Thousand Splinters (long rest, 1 minute).** You can mark up to 5 creatures at once.

name: Fjaðrfall
md:
*Feather-Fall.* **Holder:** Macsen Pritchard. **Idol:** Dafydd Gam. **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** Every Agincourt fletcher swore the grey goose feather carried the arrow further than any other.

**Blueprint, Goose Feather (at will).** Your arrows' range increases by 50 feet and their flight is silent to hearing beyond 30 feet. **Parts.** *Landing Light:* arrows that miss do not break and can be recalled to your hand once per turn.

name: Ǫxulskot
idol: The Marksman of the Long Line
md:
*Axis-Shot.* **Holder:** Tomasz Wrona. **Idol:** The Marksman of the Long Line. **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A marksman in a border war was said to fire along a single unbroken line, so that anything standing on it fell, whether ten paces away or a mile. Soldiers across a continent still argue about how many stood on that line. Suggested Idol: The Marksman of the Long Line.

**Blueprint, Along the Axis (at will).** Ranged weapon attack, range 600 feet, 2d10 piercing damage, using the rifle's own ammunition, which the Fable provides. The bearer names a straight line through themselves and one target. The shot has no disadvantage at long range and ignores half cover. It also passes through the target and strikes every other creature on that line within range; the bearer makes one attack roll and compares it to each creature's AC. **Parts.** *Through Anything:* Along the Axis ignores total cover from nonmagical objects and passes through walls and obstacles up to 1 foot thick. *Horizon Line:* Along the Axis has a range of 1 mile with no disadvantage at long range, and the shot cannot be deflected or redirected. **Maxim, Axis Break (long rest, 1 minute).** Redraws Along the Axis. The shot flies the whole length of the line to the horizon. Every creature within 5 miles on the line makes a Dexterity save, taking 8d6 piercing damage on a failure and half on a success, and the bullet ignores all cover (4th-level effect). **Chant.** "By the Marksman of the Long Line, I ask that the shot hold true. Ǫxulskot."

name: Viftuskot
idol: Nasu no Yoichi, "The Fan-Shooter of Yashima."
md:
*Fan-Shot.* **Holder:** Okiku Tsubaki. **Idol:** Nasu no Yoichi, "The Fan-Shooter of Yashima." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** From the deck of a rolling boat, a young archer was challenged to hit a fan on a pole across the waves, and prayed to the gods of the sea that he would not shame himself. He hit it.

**Blueprint, Rolling Deck (at will).** You ignore penalties for firing from an unstable surface or while moving at full speed, and you may call a shot at a small object (a fan, a rope, a lock) as a free part of an attack. **Parts.** *Brief Prayer:* once per short rest you can reroll a missed attack.

name: Slöngvusteinn
md:
*Sling-Stone.* **Holder:** Tito Valdés. **Idol:** Annie Oakley, "Little Sure Shot." **Burden** 1, **level** 1.

**Story.** Small as she was, men said no one her size could handle a rifle. Annie Oakley shot the larger targets down anyway.

**Blueprint, Giant's Aim (at will).** Add 1d4 to attack and damage rolls with a sling against a creature larger than you.

name: Sigrvegari
md:
*Conqueror of Hearts.* **Holder:** Nieth Mesu Caesar. **Idol:** Cleopatra VII, "The Barren Empress." **Burden** 5, **level** 11.

**Story.** The tale is that she ruled by wanting a thing and the world answering. The Fable is her great golden staff together with the tools that preserved her body after death.

**Blueprint, Sovereign Command (action, short rest).** Strike a creature with the staff (or point it, range 60 feet). It must pass a Charisma save or become charmed for 1 minute, obeying your commands as if you were its ruler. It repeats the save when it takes damage. **Parts, the Canopic Tools.** Each extends Sovereign Command to one function of the charmed body. *Hook of the Mind:* the creature forgets the last minute when the charm ends. *Knife of the Heart:* it cannot lie to you. *Bowl of the Breath:* it cannot speak a word you forbid. *Scoop of the Sight:* it sees only what you describe. *Linen of the Skin:* it cannot be healed by anyone but you while charmed. **Maxim, Barren Throne (long rest, 1 minute).** The charm no longer ends on damage, and the staff can command up to three creatures at once. **Signature Part, The Wish Is Granted.** Once per long rest, a request you make of a charmed creature is carried out even if it would be harmful, but the creature remembers who asked. **Price.** You must name the creature you are commanding. You cannot command what you cannot name.

name: Gelder
md:
*Barren Vow.* **Holder:** Al Munir Caesar. **Idol:** Arsinoe IV, "The Rival Sister" (proposed). **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A younger sister swore no child of hers would ever take the throne, and the sand kept the oath for her.

**Blueprint, Sandhand (action, at will).** Shape up to 10 cubic feet of loose sand or dust within 30 feet: a wall, a fist, a snare, a step. **Parts.** *Barren Ground:* nothing planted in sand you have shaped will grow for a day. *Oath-Dry:* creatures you have shaped sand around are scented by it and can be tracked.

name: Ráðblær
md:
*Counsel-Veil.* **Holder:** Meru Phalen. **Idol:** Cleopatra, "The Barren Empress." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** The queen heard every whisper in her court and answered each with the right word.

**Blueprint, Whisper to the Throne (bonus action, at will).** Choose an ally within 60 feet; only they hear your words, and they gain advantage on their next ability check or save. **Parts.** *Measured Cubits:* you always know the exact distance and height of anything in sight. *Ointment Hand:* the ally also regains 1d4 hit points. **Maxim, The Vizier's Hour (long rest, 1 minute).** The Blueprint reaches every ally who can hear you, not only one.

name: Blævængr
md:
*Breeze-Wing.* **Holder:** Sera Beranice. **Idol:** Berenice II, "The Hair-Giver." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A queen cut her hair as a vow for her husband's safe return, and the gods lifted the lock into the sky as a constellation.

**Blueprint, Fan of Vows (action, short rest).** Sweep the fan blade in a 30-foot cone: creatures take 6d6 slashing damage (Dexterity half) and are pushed 15 feet. **Parts.** *Lock of Hair:* each creature damaged leaves a sky-bright thread you can follow. *Shed Strands:* wind from the fan snuffs flames and dispels fog in the cone. **Maxim, Constellation (long rest, 1 minute).** The cone becomes a 60-foot line of cutting wind that ignores cover.

name: Tvíbrandr
idol: Mark Antony, "Her General and Her Last Love."
md:
*Two Blades.* **Holder:** Shars Cellar. **Idol:** Mark Antony, "Her General and Her Last Love." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** Mark Antony, a general with a blade in each hand, offered terms to the men he could have killed.

**Blueprint, Mercy or Edge (bonus action, at will).** Each scimitar is set to either lethal or nonlethal each turn; nonlethal strikes still deal full damage but cannot drop a foe below 1 hit point. **Parts.** *Physician's Offer:* a creature you spared grants you advantage once on a roll against its allies. *Two Hands, One Oath:* off-hand strikes add your Dexterity modifier. **Maxim, Sultan's Verdict (long rest, 1 minute).** Both scimitars can strike as a reaction when you are attacked.

name: Sefkróna
md:
*Reed Crown.* **Holder:** Philos Fendral. **Idol:** Cleopatra, "The Barren Empress." **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** Cleopatra took both crowns of Egypt and wore them until the court believed it was hers by right.

**Blueprint, Crowned in Reeds (action, short rest).** Declare a title for yourself for 1 minute. You gain a +2 bonus to AC and saves, and creatures of lesser level must succeed on a Wisdom save to attack you. **Parts.** *False Beard:* you can alter your apparent age and sex at will. *Double Crown:* the Blueprint can be applied to an ally instead, once per long rest. **Maxim, Every Monument (long rest, 1 minute).** Your title is unchallengeable by anyone below you in level, and attackers of any level have disadvantage. **Signature Part, The Beard Is Real.** Anything you disguise yourself as, you are, for the purposes of detection spells, until dawn. **Price.** You must state your title aloud before wearing it, and anyone who denies it loudly enough ends the effect.

name: Sefkörfa
md:
*Reed Basket.* **Holder:** Ineni the Reedcutter. **Idol:** Eratosthenes, "The Measurer of the Earth." **Burden** 1, **level** 1.

**Story.** The librarian Eratosthenes sent his sums downriver in a reed basket that never sank.

**Blueprint, Safe on the River (action, at will).** Create a small floating basket that cannot sink and carries one Small creature or object safely down any current. No one finds it unless it is looked for.

name: Bókhlöða
md:
*Book-Hall.* **Holder:** Kallias of Alexandria. **Idol:** Eratosthenes, "The Measurer of the Earth." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A librarian measured the circumference of the world with a shadow and a well, and was right within a few percent.

**Blueprint, Shadow and Well (action, long rest).** You instantly learn the exact direction and distance to a named location you have visited or been told about. **Parts.** *Catalog Mind:* you can recite any book you have read. *Quiet Stacks:* nobody in 20 feet of you can be heard by anyone outside it.

name: Smyrslsvefn
md:
*Ointment-Sleep.* **Holder:** Neferet-Ka. **Idol:** Tutankhamun, "The Boy King." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A young king was buried so well that thousands of years later he looked asleep.

**Blueprint, Preserved (action, short rest).** Touch a creature or corpse; it enters stasis for up to 24 hours, taking no harm, aging not at all, and unaffected by poison and disease. **Parts.** *Gilded Mask:* a creature in stasis cannot be detected by any sense. *Canopic Jar:* an organ removed from a corpse is stored indefinitely and can be returned. **Maxim, Mummy's Breath (long rest, 1 minute).** The stasis becomes instant and stops time for the creature for 1 minute, ending when you choose.

name: Sólskífa
md:
*Sun Disc.* **Holder:** Bakenkhons (Einherjar). **Idol:** Akhenaten, "The Heretic Pharaoh." **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** A king declared one god, the sun disc, and demanded the world turn to face it. Many said it was heresy, and his own name was struck from the walls.

**Blueprint, One Light (action, long rest).** A disc of sunlight burns over you for 1 minute. Radiant light fills a 60-foot radius; undead and Lost in it take 3d8 radiant damage each turn and have disadvantage on attacks. **Parts.** *No Other Gods:* spells and abilities of other beings cast in the light have disadvantage. *Erased Name:* you cannot be named or tracked by any magic while the disc burns. **Maxim, Aten Triumphant (long rest, 1 minute).** The light forces creatures of all kinds to make a Wisdom save or kneel until your next turn. **Signature Part, A Seat in Valhalla.** Because he is Einherjar, the disc may be called through the Valhalla gate by any clan member of Hatshepsut's line, once per long rest. **Price.** The Fable only burns where the disc can be seen. Fog, darkness, and cover end it.

name: Ársæll
md:
*Blessed Year.* **Holder:** Domenico Galafero. **Idol:** Lorenzo de' Medici, "The Magnificent." **Burden** 5, **level** 11.

**Story.** A banker ruled a republic by lending, giving, and commissioning, until the whole city prospered because of what he spent on it.

**Blueprint, Open Hand (action, long rest).** Each ally within 60 feet gains temporary hit points equal to five times your proficiency bonus and one extra use of a short-rest ability. **Parts.** *Patronage:* anyone you have paid or fed in the last day gains advantage on saves against fear. *Magnificent Table:* a feast you host restores all allies' hit points and ends exhaustion. **Maxim, A Golden Age (long rest, 1 minute).** Open Hand triggers again at the start of each of your turns. **Signature Part, Every Seat Is Paid For.** Clan members within 120 feet cannot be separated from you by teleportation or banishment you did not allow. **Price.** You must give something of real worth away in the chant, to a person you can name.

name: Ättestupa
idol: Dante Galafero himself (epithet to be set)
md:
*The Ancestor Cliff.* **Holder:** Dante Galafero. **Idol:** Dante Galafero himself (epithet to be set). **Burden** 2, **level** 1. **Form:** a gauntlet that takes the place of Dante's lost arm.

**Story.** Dante lost his arm shielding a young boy from a draugr and kept fighting until the boy was clear. The boy told it, and so did everyone who saw it, until the story was real enough to become the gauntlet that now takes the arm's place.

**Blueprint, Step Between (reaction, short rest).** When an ally or a child within 5 feet is hit by an attack, you may move into the attack's path and take it instead, with resistance to the damage. **Parts.** *The Hand That Remains:* the gauntlet cannot be disarmed, severed, or removed against your will, and acts as a fully working hand. *Draugr's Bane:* the gauntlet's strikes deal an extra 1d6 radiant damage to undead and Lost.

name: Breyhjálmr
md:
*Broad Helm.* **Holder:** Leonardo Coraggioso. **Idol:** Leonardo da Vinci, "The Universal Man" (proposed). **Burden** 3, **level** 3. **Form:** a shield. The name is old and the shield is a shield; it carries no helm.

**Story.** As a boy, an artist was asked to paint a shield and covered it with a monster so lifelike that his own father ran from it. He also designed war machines that split into pieces for soldiers to carry.

**Blueprint, Painted Shield (reaction, at will).** While you hold the shield, you gain +2 AC, and once per round you may turn a melee attack against you into a miss. **Parts.** *Sunder (action, once):* the shield permanently splits into up to five shards. Each becomes a separate Uncommon shield Fable (Burden 2) in the hands of an ally you choose, with the Blueprint *Shard Guard* (+1 AC, and its bearer can share that bonus with an adjacent ally as a reaction). Once split, the shards never rejoin. *Shared Battle-Line:* while any shard exists, you know where each one is and whether its bearer is in danger. **Maxim, Medusa's Face (long rest, 1 minute).** The painted monster on the shield wakes; creatures within 30 feet that can see it must pass a Wisdom save or be frightened. This works only while the shield is whole.

name: Ljúrráð
md:
*Cunning-Counsel.* **Holder:** Amadeo Feterola. **Idol:** Niccolò Machiavelli, "The Secretary." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A civil servant wrote a short book about how rulers actually behave, and it was condemned for decades by people who then followed it.

**Blueprint, Useful Lie (action, short rest).** A creature you speak to must pass a Wisdom save or believe a falsehood you state, up to one sentence, for an hour. The belief breaks if the creature takes damage. **Parts.** *Feared and Loved:* you can choose whether the creature fears you or likes you when it believes the lie. *The Prince's Mask:* detect thoughts and similar magic reveal only what you want them to. **Maxim, Better to Be Feared (long rest, 1 minute).** Useful Lie becomes a command the creature follows exactly, once.

name: Blindhertogi
md:
*Blind Duke.* **Holder:** Isabetta Contarini. **Idol:** Amerigo Vespucci, "The Florentine Navigator." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** Amerigo Vespucci's navigators mapped coasts they could not see, by stars and the sound of water.

**Blueprint, Sight Without Eyes (at will).** You have blindsight within 30 feet and cannot be blinded. **Parts.** *Navigator's Ear:* you always know true north and the depth of any water you float on. *Old Doge:* aging effects against you are halved. **Maxim, Fleet of Many Ships (long rest, 1 minute).** Blindsight extends to 120 feet and shares with every ally who can hear you.

name: Ulfynja
md:
*She-Wolf.* **Holder:** Fiammetta Orsolini. **Idol:** Caterina Sforza, "The Tiger of Forlì." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A noblewoman held her castle after her enemies took her children, and refused to yield even when they threatened to kill them.

**Blueprint, Hold the Keep (action, long rest).** Raise a stone redoubt in a 40-foot square: walls 20 feet high, one door, an arrow-slit on every side. It lasts 1 hour and allies inside have three-quarters cover. **Parts.** *Children Are Safe:* allies inside cannot be charmed or frightened. *Open Gate:* the door recognizes you and your allies and no one else. **Maxim, Tiger's Den (long rest, 1 minute).** The redoubt strikes at enemies that touch it for 4d6 piercing damage.

name: Stafrmót
md:
*Letter-Mold.* **Holder:** Tiberio Basso. **Idol:** Aldus Manutius, "The Printer of Venice." **Burden** 1, **level** 1.

**Story.** Aldus Manutius cast type so small and even that every page came out the same.

**Blueprint, Pressed Page (action, at will).** Touch a page of writing; a perfect copy appears on any blank page within reach.

name: Málaðr
md:
*The Painted.* **Holder:** Ginevra Moretti. **Idol:** Michelangelo, "The Divine One." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** Michelangelo freed figures from stone, and his apprentices said he could do the same with a blade.

**Blueprint, Draw the Blade (action, at will).** Paint a weapon on any surface; draw it out as a real, mundane weapon that lasts 1 hour. **Parts.** *True Pigment:* the weapon's damage type can be changed at drawing. *Signed Work:* the weapon returns to the canvas if lost. **Maxim, Gallery (long rest, 1 minute).** You can draw up to five weapons at once, each +1.

name: Eitrbikarr
md:
*Poison Cup.* **Holder:** Cesare Lunardi. **Idol:** Lucrezia Borgia, "The Poisoner's Daughter." **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** The rumor said every banquet she hosted had one cup that mattered, and no one could ever say which.

**Blueprint, Cup at the Feast (action, long rest).** Choose a creature within 60 feet. It must pass a Constitution save or become poisoned and take 8d6 poison damage over the next minute. **Parts.** *Ring of Hollow Stone:* you are immune to poison. *Slow Draught:* the creature does not know it was affected for an hour. **Maxim, The Whole Table (long rest, 1 minute).** The cup affects up to six creatures you can see. **Signature Part, No One Knows Which.** A creature poisoned by the cup cannot tell who gave it. **Price.** You must drink first. You take half the damage, with a save to end it.

name: Vápnhamr
md:
*Weapon-Skin.* **Holder:** Orsola Bellandi. **Idol:** The Captain of Every Blade. **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A mercenary captain was said to always have the right weapon in her hand, whatever the fight needed. Her company and the towns that hired them still tell it. Suggested Idol: The Captain of Every Blade.

**Blueprint, Many Faces (bonus action).** The weapon becomes any nonmagical weapon the bearer is proficient with, using that weapon's damage, properties and size. It can change shape once per turn at no cost, and always counts as the weapon it currently is. **Parts.** *Borrowed Edge:* Many Faces can copy more than plain weapons. After the bearer has seen or touched a weapon, the Fable can take its shape and one of its special properties for 1 hour, including a +1 bonus or a magical damage type, but not its other magical abilities. *Any Hand:* the bearer is proficient with any form Many Faces takes, and the weapon can also become a shield or a tool of weapon size. **Chant.** "By the Captain of Every Blade, I ask for the right weapon for this fight. Vápnhamr."

name: Vandlætari
md:
*The Zealous One.* **Holder:** Simon Caesonia (Einherjar). **Idol:** Simon the Zealot. **Burden** 5, **level** 11.

**Story.** A follower of a teacher was remembered by a single word: zealous. The tradition says he gave everything to a cause and was killed for it far from home.

**Blueprint, Consuming Zeal (bonus action, short rest).** For 1 minute you cannot be frightened, charmed, or turned from your stated aim; you gain temporary hit points equal to your level times three, and your weapon attacks deal an extra 2d8 radiant damage against anything that opposes the aim. **Parts.** *Single Word:* a creature that hears you swear your aim cannot lie about its own intent for a minute. *Distant Grave:* if you die away from home, your body vanishes and your Fable returns to the clan's keeping. **Maxim, Martyr's Hour (long rest, 1 minute).** The effect extends to every clan member within 60 feet who shares your aim. **Signature Part, Killed for the Cause.** If you are reduced to 0 hit points while Consuming Zeal is active, you may spend your reaction to strike with a final attack that cannot miss. **Price.** You must announce your aim aloud and keep to it. If you turn from it, the Fable goes dark until dawn.

name: Ástklæði
md:
*Cherished Garment.* **Holder:** Warren Gramblin (fallen). **Idol:** Simon the Zealot. **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** Simon the Zealot gave his cloak to a stranger in the cold, and was killed far from home.

**Blueprint, Half a Cloak (reaction, short rest).** When an adjacent ally would take damage, you share half of it with yourself. **Parts.** *Warmth Given:* the ally also gains resistance to cold for an hour. The Fable now sits idle until a new bearer accepts it by Inheritance.

name: Ljósormr
md:
*Light-Worm.* **Holder:** Tristan Cryer. **Idol:** The Lantern-Keeper of the Marsh. **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A lamplighter in a marsh village walked into the dark each night and came back with her lantern full of fireflies, until the village swore the dark itself was afraid of her. Told across a city and its marshes. Suggested Idol: The Lantern-Keeper of the Marsh.

**Blueprint, Lantern Swarm (action).** The staff drinks light and sheds it as bugs. Drain nonmagical light within 30 feet, leaving the area dark. For every 5-foot square of light drained, a lightning bug forms inside the staff, up to twice the bearer's proficiency bonus, and the staff makes 1 more at each long rest if it is below that maximum. As an action, release up to proficiency bonus + 2 bugs. Each flies to a point within 60 feet and explodes in a 5-foot radius for 2d6 lightning damage (Dexterity save for half). A released bug is spent. **Parts.** *Light Eater:* Lantern Swarm can also drain magical light and light-based spells of 3rd level or lower within 30 feet, dimming or ending them, and the staff makes a bug from each. *Chain Spark:* each exploding bug arcs to a second creature within 15 feet of its target for half damage. **Maxim, Swarm Night (long rest, 1 minute).** Redraws Lantern Swarm. The staff drains all light within 60 feet and doubles every bug inside it. The whole swarm is released in a cloud for 1 minute; at the start of each of the bearer's turns each bug explodes on a creature of the bearer's choice in the cloud for 3d6 lightning damage (Dexterity save for half) (4th-level effect). **Chant.** "By the Lantern-Keeper of the Marsh, I ask for the dark to light up. Ljósormr."

name: Hvítrós
md:
*White Rose.* **Holder:** Dietlinde "Linde" König. **Idol:** Simon the Zealot. **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** Simon and the Zealots refused Rome, and said so aloud where all could hear.

**Blueprint, Say It Aloud (action, short rest).** Everything you say for 1 minute is heard and understood by every creature in 120 feet, whatever language or barrier. Allies there have advantage on saves against being charmed, frightened, or commanded. **Parts.** *Leaflets:* a message you speak is copied onto paper in the hands of anyone you name. *The Court Heard:* a creature that tries to silence you takes 4d6 psychic damage. **Maxim, Someone Had to (long rest, 1 minute).** The effect also dispels any magical compulsion on allies in range.

name: Hrópandi
idol: John the Baptist, "The Voice in the Wilderness."
md:
*The Crying Out.* **Holder:** Ansgar Voll. **Idol:** John the Baptist, "The Voice in the Wilderness." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A hermit shouted that someone greater was coming, and a great many came out into the desert to hear him.

**Blueprint, Cry in the Wilderness (action, short rest).** Let out a shout that carries a mile. Creatures within 60 feet take 5d8 thunder damage (Constitution half); creatures farther away hear it clearly as a call to come to you. **Parts.** *Make Straight:* difficult terrain on the way to you vanishes for allies who answer. *Camel Hair:* you have resistance to cold and heat while in the wilds. **Maxim, Prepare the Way (long rest, 1 minute).** All allies who hear you can move to you as a reaction, ignoring terrain.

name: Sægarpr
md:
*Sea-Warrior.* **Holder:** Maren Holt. **Idol:** Saint Brendan, "The Navigator." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A monk set out in a leather boat to find an island of the blessed and found a great fish he took for an island.

**Blueprint, Leather Boat (action, at will).** Make a small boat out of hide that rides on any surface, including sand, snow, and lava, and carries up to six creatures. **Parts.** *Island of the Blessed:* the boat is a safe place; no creature aboard can be surprised. *Good Fish:* it can dive and carry its passengers beneath water for 10 minutes. **Maxim, The Long Voyage (long rest, 1 minute).** The boat crosses a distance of your choosing, up to 10 miles, in the time it takes to speak.

name: Grasagaldr
idol: Hildegard of Bingen, "The Sibyl of the Rhine."
md:
*Herb-Charm.* **Holder:** Vesna Kolar. **Idol:** Hildegard of Bingen, "The Sibyl of the Rhine." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** An abbess wrote down visions, music, and cures, and said the green force in all living things was the greatest power.

**Blueprint, Greening (action, at will).** Touch a plant or soil to make it flower and grow in seconds. An ally you touch regains 2d6 hit points. **Parts.** *Viriditas:* creatures standing in your garden have advantage on saves against poison. *Seed Memory:* a plant you grow remembers a message you whisper to it. **Maxim, Green Force (long rest, 1 minute).** All plants in 60 feet grow, entangle your foes, and heal your allies each turn.

name: Ferðafótr
md:
*Traveler's Foot.* **Holder:** Jorun Eskil. **Idol:** Ibn Battuta, "The Traveler." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A man set out to make one pilgrimage and kept walking for nearly thirty years, writing it all down.

**Blueprint, Long Road (at will).** You and up to four allies cross a day's march without tiring; forced marches do not cause exhaustion. **Parts.** *Memory of Roads:* you never forget a road you have walked. *Welcome Guest:* strangers you meet in a settlement are friendly on your first conversation.

name: Dýrabróðir
md:
*Beast-Brother.* **Holder:** Wim Teague. **Idol:** Saint Francis of Assisi, "The Beast-Brother." **Burden** 1, **level** 1.

**Story.** A beggar-friar is said to have preached to birds, and talked a wolf out of eating a town.

**Blueprint, Sparrow's Sermon (action, at will).** You can speak with and understand beasts of Small size or smaller, and they will not attack you unless provoked.

name: Fjǫtrbrjótr
md:
*Fetter-Breaker.* **Holder:** Tarhun Ballo. **Idol:** Spartacus, "The Gladiator Who Rose." **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** A slave in the arena broke out with a handful of others, and an army of the enslaved followed him over the mountains.

**Blueprint, Break the Chain (action, short rest).** Touch a restraint, cage, chain, or compulsion; it breaks. You can also free a creature from imprisonment effects, including magical ones of 6th level or lower. **Parts.** *Bound No More:* freed creatures gain 2d10 temporary hit points and advantage on their next saving throw. *Many Hands:* up to six creatures freed at once can act immediately, outside initiative. **Maxim, The Whole Camp (long rest, 1 minute).** Every restraint within 120 feet, friend or foe, breaks at your word. **Signature Part, Slave to None.** You and all allies you touch cannot be held, grappled, or paralyzed for 1 minute. **Price.** You must set free at least one creature each time. If you cannot, the Fable refuses you.

name: Ensis
idol: King Arthur, "The Once and Future King" (proposed, since the sword is canon and its source is not)
md:
*The Sword.* **Holder:** Amadel, the High Mother. **Idol:** King Arthur, "The Once and Future King" (proposed, since the sword is canon and its source is not). **Burden** 7, **level** Story (a bearer must be judged worthy by the High Guard).

**Story.** A boy drew a sword from a stone that no strong man could move, was crowned for it, and is said to be only sleeping.

**Blueprint, The Rightful Edge (bonus action, at will).** The sword deals 6d10 radiant damage to anything it strikes that is unworthy to stand against its bearer (the Lost, tyrants, oathbreakers). Against any other creature it deals normal weapon damage but never harms the innocent. **Parts.** *Scabbard of Healing:* while the sword is sheathed, you cannot lose hit points from bleeding, poison, or disease. *The Stone:* the sword can be driven into any surface and cannot be removed by anyone but its bearer. *Round Table:* up to twelve allies sitting at a meal with you cannot be charmed, frightened, or lied to. **Maxim, Once and Future (long rest, 1 minute).** You and every ally within 60 feet return to full hit points the first time they would drop to 0 this minute. **Signature Part, First of the Halr.** The sword recognizes its bearer's peers; a creature touched by the blade learns whether they are worthy to be Halr. **Price.** The bearer swears a public oath each year, and breaking it makes the sword too heavy to lift.

name: Dómsetr
md:
*Judgment Seat.* **Holder:** Leonce Enguerrand. **Idol:** Solomon, "The Wise Judge." **Burden** 5, **level** 11.

**Story.** Two women claimed one child, and the king ordered it cut in two. The one who cried out to spare it was named the mother.

**Blueprint, Verdict (action, long rest).** Name a charge against a creature within 60 feet. It must pass a Wisdom save or be bound by your sentence for 24 hours: it cannot break the terms you set, and if it does, it takes 6d10 psychic damage. **Parts.** *Two Claimants:* if two creatures make opposing claims before you, the one telling the truth feels it and the other cannot lie convincingly. *Cut the Child:* you can force a creature to reveal what it values most. **Maxim, The Last Word (long rest, 1 minute).** Your sentence cannot be resisted, dispelled, or altered by anything below 9th level. **Signature Part, Seated.** While you sit, you cannot be moved by anything short of a Hand-level force. **Price.** A Verdict must be stated plainly and be fair on its face. A cruel or false charge turns on the speaker.

name: Lǫgsteinn
md:
*Law-Stone.* **Holder:** Lex Konstal. **Idol:** Hammurabi, "The Stele-Carver." **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** A king had the laws carved in stone and set up in public, so that no one could claim not to know them.

**Blueprint, Written Law (action, long rest).** Carve a rule into a surface or into the air; for 1 hour, all creatures in 60 feet who can read or hear it must obey it or take 5d8 psychic damage per round of breaking it. The rule must be a single sentence and cannot compel harm. **Parts.** *Eye for an Eye:* any creature that harms another within the area takes the same damage. *Public Stele:* the law is known to every creature that enters the area. **Maxim, Stele of Ages (long rest, 1 minute).** The rule lasts a full day and cannot be unwritten except by you. **Signature Part, Court Is Open.** In your presence a creature cannot be forced to testify against itself by magic or other means. **Price.** Every Written Law must be one you would obey yourself.

name: blástr
md:
*The Blast.* **Holder:** Sol-An Taliar. **Idol:** Roland, "The Horn of Roncesvalles" (proposed). **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** A knight refused to sound his horn until it was too late, then blew it so hard his temples burst, and the whole army turned back.

**Blueprint, Olifant (action, short rest).** Sound a blast audible across any layer; creatures within 60 feet take 6d8 thunder damage (Constitution half) and are deafened. Allies within a mile know where you stand. **Parts.** *Pass Guard:* you can seal a narrow place against passage for 1 minute, enemies must pass a Strength save to cross it. *Brother Calls:* an ally who hears the blast may teleport 30 feet to your side as a reaction. **Maxim, Too Late (long rest, 1 minute).** The blast comes from every ally at once, doubling its radius and damage. **Signature Part, The Sound Is Seen.** The blast also leaves a mark on the sky that shows your location for an hour to anyone you choose. **Price.** You cannot blow the horn the first time an enemy appears, only the second time.

name: Stǫðvun
md:
*Halt.* **Holder:** Odo Pell. **Idol:** The Warden of the Crossing. **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A crossing warden in one town held up a column of riders with a hand-painted sign after a child was nearly run down. The town still obeys that sign, and nobody else does. Suggested Idol: The Warden of the Crossing.

**Blueprint, Halt (action, twice per short rest).** Point the sign at a creature within 30 feet. It makes a Wisdom save or its speed becomes 0 and it cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn. **Parts.** *Right of Way:* Halt can be aimed at a thing instead of a creature: a thrown object, a projectile in flight, or a moving vehicle or construct. It stops dead, and a ranged attack halted this way misses. *Red Light:* a creature held by Halt is held for 1 minute instead, cannot fly, teleport or burrow while held, and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. **Chant.** "By the Warden of the Crossing, I ask that you go no further. Stǫðvun."

name: Valreið
md:
*Ride of the Slain.* **Holder:** Ysolde Varga. **Idol:** El Cid, "The Champion." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A great knight died during a siege, and his men strapped his body to his horse and sent him out, and the enemy broke and ran.

**Blueprint, Dead Man's Charge (reaction, long rest).** When you would drop to 0 hit points, you do not fall; you ride out and make one full attack round against every enemy within 30 feet, then collapse. **Parts.** *The Horse Knows:* your mount takes no damage while the charge lasts. *Banner of the Dead:* enemies who see you ride out must save or be frightened for 1 minute. **Maxim, Even in Death (long rest, 1 minute).** The charge can be triggered twice.

name: Gullstóll
idol: Yaa Asantewaa, "The Defender of the Golden Stool."
md:
*Golden Stool.* **Holder:** Kofi Asare. **Idol:** Yaa Asantewaa, "The Defender of the Golden Stool." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** When a king was exiled, a queen mother raised an army to protect the stool that held the soul of her people, and refused to hand it over.

**Blueprint, The Seat Is Not Yours (action, short rest).** Set the stool down; a 30-foot aura forms around it for 1 minute. Hostile creatures cannot willingly move closer to it unless they pass a Charisma save each turn, and allies in the aura cannot be moved against their will. **Parts.** *The Nation's Soul:* if the stool is taken, you instantly know where it is. *Unbowed:* allies in the aura have advantage on saves against fear. **Maxim, Whole People (long rest, 1 minute).** The aura becomes 90 feet and allies deal an extra die of damage.

name: Landamæri
md:
*The Border.* **Holder:** Ilse Brandt. **Idol:** Hadrian, "The Wall-Builder." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** An emperor walked the edge of his empire and ordered a wall built the whole length, so that people knew where the border was.

**Blueprint, Draw the Line (action, short rest).** Mark a line up to 120 feet long; creatures of your choice cannot cross it without succeeding on a Strength save, and crossing without leave alerts you. **Parts.** *Milecastles:* you can leave a ward behind at any point on the line to hold it. *Vallum:* the line extends underground by 10 feet. **Maxim, Edge of the World (long rest, 1 minute).** The line becomes a wall of force, 120 feet long, 20 feet high.

name: Sagnnótt
md:
*Story-Night.* **Holder:** Hamid Zarrin. **Idol:** Scheherazade, "The Thousand and One Nights." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A woman delayed her own execution by telling a king a story each night and stopping at the best part.

**Blueprint, Stay Your Hand (action, short rest).** While you tell a story aloud, a creature that can hear you must pass a Wisdom save or be unable to attack or leave, as long as you keep talking (up to 1 minute per turn spent). **Parts.** *To Be Continued:* you can stop mid-sentence and resume later; the creature wants to hear the rest. *Many Voices:* characters in your story manifest as illusions you control. **Maxim, A Thousand Nights (long rest, 1 minute).** The story can capture up to six creatures at once.

name: Næturreið
md:
*Night Ride.* **Holder:** Edda Roth. **Idol:** Paul Revere, "The Midnight Rider." **Burden** 1, **level** 1.

**Story.** A silversmith rode through the night to warn the countryside that the army was coming.

**Blueprint, Alarm Bell (action, at will).** Send a message or alarm up to a mile; every ally you choose hears a clear bell and knows the direction of the danger.

name: Reikningr
md:
*The Reckoning.* **Holder:** Charles Carmine. **Idol:** King Midas, "The Golden Touch." **Burden** 7, **level** Story (a holder must be named by the bank's board).

**Story.** A king wished that all he touched would turn to gold, and learned too late what that meant when his food and his daughter turned to metal.

**Blueprint, Everything Has a Price (action, at will).** Name a creature or object you can see and a price. The target must either pay it within a minute, or take 10d10 force damage and be unable to leave your sight until it does. You cannot name a price the target cannot pay in some form. **Parts.** *Golden Touch:* a mundane object you touch becomes gold, and gold you touch becomes any mundane object of equal weight. *Interest:* a price unpaid by dawn doubles. *The Ledger Remembers:* every debt entered cannot be forgotten, forgiven, or disputed by magic below 9th level. *Daughter of Gold:* a creature turned to gold is preserved safely and can be restored. **Maxim, Reckoning Day (long rest, 1 minute).** Every unpaid debt in 120 feet is called due at once. **Signature Part, Credit Is Faith.** Anyone who has agreed to a debt with you is bound to you by a mark they cannot remove. **Price.** The Ledger is a two-way book. Every debt you incur in the chant must be written in, and you may not refuse payment.

name: Lykilorð
idol: Ali Baba, "The Woodcutter of the Forty."
md:
*Password.* **Holder:** Mansour Haddad. **Idol:** Ali Baba, "The Woodcutter of the Forty." **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** A poor man overheard thieves speak two words at a cave, and the stone rolled aside. Greed took his brother, and wit saved him.

**Blueprint, Open (action, at will).** Speak a word and any lock, door, or seal within 60 feet opens, including magical ones of 6th level or lower. **Parts.** *Cave Mouth:* you can open a doorway in any solid surface up to 10 feet thick for 1 minute. *Forty Thieves:* the opening can be sealed behind you so that only you can pass. **Maxim, Open Sesame (long rest, 1 minute).** Everything within 120 feet that is closed opens at once. **Signature Part, Wood for Burning.** You can tell what is behind any door you open before you step through. **Price.** The word must be spoken in full and aloud.

name: Tvíbók
md:
*Double Book.* **Holder:** Livia Corvino. **Idol:** Luca Pacioli, "Father of Accounting." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A monk wrote down how to keep two columns for every sum, so that every gain had a matching loss and no error could hide.

**Blueprint, Debit and Credit (reaction, short rest).** When a creature within 60 feet takes damage or gains hit points, you may move that amount to another creature you can see within 60 feet. **Parts.** *Balance Sheet:* you know every creature's current hit points within 60 feet. *No Error Hides:* illusions and disguises cast by creatures in your sight have disadvantage on their saves to be detected. **Maxim, Books Closed (long rest, 1 minute).** Any effect applied in 60 feet is reversed at the end of your turn.

name: Botnlauspungr
md:
*Bottomless Purse.* **Holder:** Pieter van Aelst. **Idol:** Fortunatus, "The Man of the Purse." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A poor man was given a purse that always held coins, and found that the only difficulty with unlimited money is that everyone knows you have it.

**Blueprint, Always Coin (action, at will).** Draw coins from the purse; they can be thrown as thrown weapons dealing 1d8 force damage, or offered as bribes. **Parts.** *Deep Pockets:* the purse holds an unlimited number of mundane items. *Open Hand:* a creature that accepts a coin from you must pass a Wisdom save or be charmed for an hour. **Maxim, Everyone Has a Price (long rest, 1 minute).** Any creature you could reasonably bribe is automatically charmed by the first offer.

name: Flettihanzkar
md:
*Peel-Gloves.* **Holder:** Sabine Marchetti. **Idol:** The Midwinter Thief. **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A thief who robbed a duke's winter feast was said to have opened walls, floors and even guards like gifts, leaving only the paper. Told in every city on that layer. Suggested Idol: The Midwinter Thief.

**Blueprint, Unwrap (action).** Touch a surface or object and peel its outermost layer away like wrapping paper, in a sheet up to 10 feet by 10 feet. A wall is peeled to a hole 5 feet wide and 1 foot deep per use; grass, paint, dirt, carpet and cloth are peeled to the layer below. The sheet stays in one piece and can be carried or laid elsewhere. Small peels are at will. Walls and floors can be peeled three times per long rest. **Parts.** *Peel Skin:* Unwrap can be used on a living creature. It makes a Constitution save or its outer layer (armor or natural armor) comes away, reducing its AC by 3 for 1 minute. *Through the Layers:* Unwrap can peel magical barriers and wards as well as physical surfaces. It strips one layer from a barrier or ward of 3rd level or lower, opening a gap for 1 round. **Maxim, Gift Wrapped (long rest, 1 minute).** Redraws Unwrap. Everything in a 20-foot radius around the bearer is unwrapped at once. Walls and floors peel to difficult terrain, objects lose their outer layers, and creatures make a Dexterity save or have their armor peeled off (AC becomes 10 + Dexterity modifier) for 1 minute (4th-level effect). **Chant.** "By the Midwinter Thief, I ask to open what was wrapped. Flettihanzkar."

name: Lánsbréf
md:
*Letter of Credit.* **Holder:** Yusuf al-Rahim. **Idol:** Marco Datini, "The Merchant of Prato." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A merchant wrote thousands of letters to agents across the Mediterranean, moving money without moving a coin.

**Blueprint, Delivered Unseen (action, short rest).** Write a note and attach an object no heavier than 50 pounds. The object arrives with the note at a named person you know of, anywhere on the same layer. **Parts.** *Sealed Wax:* only the named recipient can open the package. *Receipt:* you learn when it has been opened. **Maxim, Bill of Exchange (long rest, 1 minute).** The package can reach any layer and arrives instantly.

name: Kattarauðr
md:
*Cat's Fortune.* **Holder:** Greta Voss. **Idol:** Dick Whittington, "The Lord Mayor's Cat." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A poor boy sent his only cat to a faraway land to catch the rats of a king, and came back rich.

**Blueprint, Mouser (action, at will).** Summon a clever cat that acts as a scout and thief, able to steal a small item unnoticed and bring it back. **Parts.** *Nine Lives:* the cat returns unharmed if it dies. *King's Rats:* it can drive off vermin from a building in an hour. **Maxim, Fortune Made (long rest, 1 minute).** The cat grows to the size of a horse and fights as a beast of challenge 4.

name: Stœkkir
md:
*Magnify.* **Holder:** Ottilie Brandhorst. **Idol:** The Scholar of Small Things. **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A scholar in a river town spent her life looking at small things through a great lens, and the town says anything she looked at long enough grew in importance. Known across the town and its guilds. Suggested Idol: The Scholar of Small Things.

**Blueprint, Magnify (action, once per short rest for creatures; at will for objects).** Hold the lens up; the bearer or an ally then throws an object through it. An object thrown through the lens grows one size category for 1 minute. A thrown weapon deals one extra damage die, and a thrown loose object up to Medium becomes a Large missile that deals 3d6 bludgeoning damage on a hit. A willing creature that steps through the lens is enlarged for 1 minute (2nd-level effect). **Parts.** *Double Size:* Magnify grows an object or creature two size categories instead of one, and a thrown weapon gains two extra damage dice. *Burning Focus:* in bright light a magnified thrown object deals an extra 2d6 fire damage and sets flammable material alight. **Chant.** "By the Scholar of Small Things, I ask to see it larger. Stœkkir."

name: Skuldabréf
md:
*Promissory Note.* **Holder:** Nils Ekberg. **Idol:** Doctor Faustus, "The Bargain-Maker." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A scholar signed a contract for twenty-four years of knowledge in exchange for his soul, and no clause of it could be escaped.

**Blueprint, Fine Print (action, short rest).** A written agreement between you and one creature is binding for a day. If either side breaks it, they take 2d6 psychic damage and the other side knows. **Parts.** *Signature Required:* the agreement only binds if both sign. *Time Clause:* it can be set to run for up to a week.

name: Smápeningr
md:
*Small Coin.* **Holder:** Mina Okafor. **Idol:** Benjamin Franklin, "A Penny Saved." **Burden** 1, **level** 1.

**Story.** A printer wrote that a penny saved is a penny earned, and a great many people believed him.

**Blueprint, Lucky Penny (reaction, long rest).** Add 1d4 to one attack roll, saving throw, or ability check after the roll.

name: Þúsundgríma
md:
*Thousand Masks.* **Holder:** Kagerō Ōtomo. **Idol:** Ishikawa Goemon, "The Prince of Thieves." **Burden** 6, **level** 17.

**Story.** A famous thief stole from the powerful, was caught after trying to steal a sword from a warlord, and was boiled alive in a cauldron, holding his young son above the oil until the last.

**Blueprint, Wear Another (action, short rest).** Don a mask and become any humanoid you have seen. You gain their appearance, voice, and one skill or proficiency they are known for, for 8 hours or until you remove it. **Parts.** *Cauldron Skin:* heat and fire deal half damage to you in any mask. *Held Above the Oil:* an ally you are shielding cannot be harmed by area effects while you stand next to them. *No Two Alike:* each mask you wear leaves no trace of the previous one. **Maxim, A Thousand Faces (long rest, 1 minute).** You can wear up to ten masks at once, acting as ten separate people with the same hit points. **Signature Part, The Prince Stole the Moon.** Once per long rest, you can steal a single ability, spell, or magic item property from a creature you touch and use it for an hour. **Price.** You cannot wear the mask of a creature you have wronged and not repaid.

name: Skuggastígr
md:
*Shadow Path.* **Holder:** Tsubasa Ikeda. **Idol:** Hattori Hanzō, "Devil Hanzō." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A shinobi captain served a shogun so faithfully that stories said he could vanish and appear anywhere a shadow fell.

**Blueprint, Step Between (bonus action, short rest).** Step from one shadow into another within 120 feet that you can see, along with up to one willing ally. **Parts.** *Silent Foot:* you make no sound when you use the step. *Devil's Eye:* you can see through the shadow you step into before you commit. **Maxim, A Hundred Shadows (long rest, 1 minute).** You can step as a bonus action every turn for the minute.

name: Brúarstaða
md:
*Bridge-Stand.* **Holder:** Daigo Mori. **Idol:** Benkei, "The Standing Death." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A warrior monk stood alone on a bridge to hold off an army, took so many arrows that he was bristling with them, and did not fall. The enemy realized he had died upright only when someone pushed him.

**Blueprint, Hold the Bridge (reaction, short rest).** While you stand in a space where only one creature can reach you at a time, you cannot be moved, knocked prone, or forced past, and you have resistance to piercing and slashing damage. **Parts.** *Quiver of Arrows:* arrows that hit you are added to your quiver. *Still Standing:* if you drop to 0 hit points while holding the bridge, you remain standing until the end of your next turn. **Maxim, A Thousand Arrows (long rest, 1 minute).** You are immune to ranged attacks.

name: Leiksvið
idol: Izumo no Okuni, "The Founder of Kabuki."
md:
*The Stage.* **Holder:** Haruka Mizuno. **Idol:** Izumo no Okuni, "The Founder of Kabuki." **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** A shrine maiden began dancing in the dry riverbed in costume, and the plays she started are still being performed.

**Blueprint, Raise the Curtain (action, long rest).** Create a 60-foot stage that lasts 10 minutes. Creatures you choose within it are assigned a role; each must pass a Wisdom save at the start of its turn or act out the role, taking only actions that fit. **Parts.** *Costume Change:* the roles you assign can include appearance changes. *Audience:* creatures outside the stage must pass a Wisdom save to leave sight of it. **Maxim, Final Act (long rest, 1 minute).** The stage collapses at your word, dealing 6d10 psychic damage to everything inside. **Signature Part, The Show Must Go On.** If you are reduced to 0 hit points on your stage, the curtain falls and you leave the stage unharmed. **Price.** You must name each actor's role aloud.

name: Húðrún
idol: The Tattooer of the Drowned Fleet
md:
*Skin-Rune.* **Holder:** Sosuke Irezumi. **Idol:** The Tattooer of the Drowned Fleet. **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A sailor-artist tattooed the whole crew of a fleet before a voyage. When the ships went down, survivors swore the marks climbed off their skin to save them and that their lost belongings came home as ink. Told across the port cities. Suggested Idol: The Tattooer of the Drowned Fleet.

**Blueprint, Real Ink (bonus action).** A tattoo lifts off the bearer's skin and becomes real for 1 hour or until the bearer takes it back (bonus action). It can be a nonmagical weapon, shield or tool of up to Medium size, or a Tiny creature (a bird, a snake) that acts on the bearer's turn with the stats of a beast of CR 0. The bearer has a number of designs equal to proficiency bonus + 2 and chooses them at a long rest. **Blueprint, Inked Away (action, at will).** Touch a nonmagical object of up to Medium size that is not worn or carried by an unwilling creature. It becomes a tattoo on the bearer's skin. The bearer can have a number of objects stored equal to the Fable's Burden. Returning one to its original form takes an action. **Parts.** *Fine Lines:* Real Ink can make designs up to Large size, and anything it creates counts as a magical +1 weapon or shield while real. *Stowaway:* stored objects cannot be found by searches, taken in a disarm or stolen, and return to the bearer after a long rest if they were separated. **Maxim, Full Sleeve (long rest, 1 minute).** Redraws Real Ink. Every design on the bearer becomes real at once for 1 minute, up to the full number of designs, and the bearer gains temporary hit points equal to their level for each tattoo that is a creature (4th-level effect). **Chant.** "By the Tattooer of the Drowned Fleet, I ask that the ink come off my skin. Húðrún."

name: Biðhefnd
md:
*Waiting-Revenge.* **Holder:** Rin Asakura. **Idol:** Ōishi Kuranosuke, "Chief of the Forty-Seven." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** After their lord was forced to die, his retainers pretended to be drunks and idlers for nearly two years, then struck on a snowy night.

**Blueprint, Patient Blade (reaction, short rest).** When a creature harms you or an ally, mark it. The next time you hit it after waiting at least an hour, the strike deals an extra 4d6 damage. **Parts.** *Feigned Idleness:* creatures you have marked read you as harmless. *Snow Night:* your first strike on a marked creature cannot be detected until it lands. **Maxim, Forty-Seven (long rest, 1 minute).** Up to six allies can mark the same target and each deals the extra damage.

name: Ósárr
md:
*The Unwounded.* **Holder:** Hiroto Kuroda. **Idol:** Honda Tadakatsu, "The Unwounded." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A general fought in more than fifty battles and was said never to have been wounded once.

**Blueprint, No Mark (reaction, at will).** Once per round, when a creature hits you, you may reduce the damage by 1d10 plus your proficiency bonus. **Parts.** *Dragonfly Cut:* your reach with a spear increases by 5 feet. *Fifty Fields:* damage reduction doubles against the first attack each combat. **Maxim, Not One Scratch (long rest, 1 minute).** The first three attacks against you each round automatically miss.

name: Bollafriðr
idol: Sen no Rikyū, "The Master of Tea."
md:
*Cup-Peace.* **Holder:** Fumiko Hara. **Idol:** Sen no Rikyū, "The Master of Tea." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A tea master taught that every meeting happens once and is never repeated, and so must be treated as a treasure.

**Blueprint, One Time, One Meeting (action, short rest).** Share a cup with up to four creatures. For an hour, they have advantage on social checks with each other and cannot draw weapons against each other. **Parts.** *Bitter Bowl:* a creature that lies while sharing the cup tastes it and is exposed to everyone at the cup.

name: Pappírsvǫrðr
md:
*Paper Guardian.* **Holder:** Kenta Ueda. **Idol:** Abe no Seimei, "The Onmyoji." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A court diviner folded paper into servants and sent them to act on his behalf.

**Blueprint, Fold the Servant (action, short rest).** Fold a sheet of paper into a Tiny creature that obeys you for an hour: it can scout, carry a message, or distract. **Parts.** *Ink Eye:* you see through the servant's eyes. *Paper Cut:* it can deal 1d6 slashing damage once.

name: Teningskast
md:
*Dice-Throw.* **Holder:** Kiyoshi Date. **Idol:** Shimizu no Jirōchō, "The Gambler-Boss." **Burden** 1, **level** 1.

**Story.** A boss of the road gamblers won the respect of a whole region by always paying what he owed.

**Blueprint, Fair Roll (reaction, long rest).** Reroll one d20 on a gambling or game-of-chance roll and take the better result.

name: Lokabók
md:
*The Last Book.* **Holder:** Orla Veyne (Acceptance). **Idol:** Orpheus, "The Mourner Who Looked Back." **Burden** 6, **level** 17.

**Story.** A musician went into the underworld for his wife, charmed even the dead, and lost her when he looked back to be sure she followed. He wandered in grief until the end.

**Blueprint, Let It End (action, short rest).** End any ongoing spell, curse, condition, or effect that you can see within 120 feet, including ones of 8th level or lower. A creature freed from an effect also loses any fear or grief tied to it. **Parts.** *Lyre's Quiet:* creatures within 30 feet are calmed (no combat, no violent intent) for 1 minute unless they pass a Wisdom save. *The Dead Listen:* you can speak with any dead creature for 10 minutes. *Do Not Look Back:* an ally you lead out of danger cannot be pursued by the thing they flee. **Maxim, The Final Page (long rest, 1 minute).** Anything you have ended cannot return for the minute, and you can end more than one effect per turn. **Signature Part, I Let Her Go.** Once per long rest, you may release a creature from any bond, oath, or geas by speaking its name. **Price.** You must have lost something to be able to end something. The first time each day you use Let It End, you give up one thing you love for an hour.

name: Heiftarbók
md:
*Book of Rage.* **Holder:** Brandt Kessel (Anger). **Idol:** Orpheus, "The Mourner Who Looked Back." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** Orpheus raged at the gods and played until the trees pulled up their roots.

**Blueprint, Wrath of Achilles (bonus action, short rest).** For 1 minute, you have advantage on all melee attacks and deal an extra 2d8 damage on each hit, but you must attack the nearest creature each turn. **Parts.** *Heel:* the first attack against you each round that hits automatically deals only half damage. *Black Rage:* you cannot be frightened or charmed while the rage burns. **Maxim, Dragging Hector (long rest, 1 minute).** A creature you reduce to 0 hit points can be dragged behind you without slowing you down, and enemies must pass a save to attack it.

name: Sorgarbók
md:
*Book of Sorrows.* **Holder:** Lucan Ashe (Depression). **Idol:** Orpheus, "The Mourner Who Looked Back." **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** Orpheus wandered the riverbanks, refusing food and company.

**Blueprint, Weight of the World (action, short rest).** Choose a creature within 60 feet. It must pass a Wisdom save or its speed becomes 0, its attack rolls have disadvantage, and it takes 3d8 psychic damage each turn. It repeats the save at the end of each turn. **Parts.** *Ashes and Sackcloth:* creatures within 30 feet cannot regain hit points while the weight lasts. *Friends Who Sit:* allies who sit with you for a minute lose a level of exhaustion. **Maxim, All Is Taken (long rest, 1 minute).** The weight affects every enemy within 60 feet. **Signature Part, Still Faithful.** You cannot be reduced below 1 hit point by psychic damage. **Price.** You gain a level of exhaustion each time the weight is used, which no rest can remove until the next dawn.

name: Trúleysi
md:
*Unbelief.* **Holder:** Thaddea Marsh (Disbelief). **Idol:** Orpheus, "The Mourner Who Looked Back." **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** Orpheus would not believe she was dead, and went down to see for himself.

**Blueprint, Put Your Finger Here (action, at will).** Touch an illusion, disguise, or glamour; it ends. Within 30 feet, you see through any disguise or false form without a check. **Parts.** *Show Me:* a creature that tries to deceive you must make a Charisma save or reveal what it is hiding. *Sure of Touch:* you can identify any magic item or effect by touching it. **Maxim, Doubting Eye (long rest, 1 minute).** All illusions and deceptions within 120 feet are ended and cannot be recast for the minute.

name: Þrír Apar
md:
*Three Apes.* **Holder:** Ichabod Finch (Denial). **Idol:** as in the Starter Catalog (The Left-Handed Carver). **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** The three wise monkeys carved over a shrine door are known across a nation and far beyond it. Suggested Idol: The Left-Handed Carver, the legendary carver said to have made them.

**Blueprint, No Evil (action; each monkey once per short rest).** One monkey covers its sense, choosing a creature within 60 feet. The creature makes a Wisdom save or suffers the effect until the end of its next turn. All three can be used in the same round on different targets. *See No Evil:* the target is blinded. *Hear No Evil:* the target is deafened and cannot hear the bearer's allies. *Speak No Evil:* the target cannot speak or cast spells with verbal components. **Parts.** *Beyond Sight:* No Evil also shuts down magical senses; See No Evil removes blindsight, darkvision and truesight, Hear No Evil removes telepathy and tremorsense, and Speak No Evil stops any ability that needs a voice, including innate spellcasting. *Lingering:* No Evil lasts 1 minute and the target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. *Spread:* other creatures within 10 feet of the target must also make the save or suffer the same effect. **Maxim, The Fourth Monkey (long rest, 1 minute).** Redraws No Evil. The hidden fourth monkey, "Do No Evil", steps forward. A creature within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save or cannot take any hostile action for 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns (6th-level effect). **Chant.** "By the Left-Handed Carver, I ask that you see, hear and say nothing. Þrír Apar."

name: Kaupbók
md:
*Bargain-Book.* **Holder:** Silas Crowe (Bargaining). **Idol:** Orpheus, "The Mourner Who Looked Back." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** Orpheus bargained with the king and queen of the dead: she may follow him out, if he does not look back.

**Blueprint, Lower the Number (reaction, short rest).** When a spell or effect with a numeric threshold affects you or an ally within 30 feet, reduce the damage, duration, or targets by half in exchange for giving up something you offer aloud. **Parts.** *Fifty to Ten:* you may repeat the haggle once more, each time cutting the effect by half again. *Open Ledger:* the offer is remembered, and you cannot renege. **Maxim, Even for Ten (long rest, 1 minute).** The effect is negated entirely for a price one tier greater.

name: Sektarbók
md:
*Book of Guilt.* **Holder:** Marguerite Dunn (Guilt). **Idol:** Orpheus, "The Mourner Who Looked Back." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** Orpheus looked back, and blamed himself forever.

**Blueprint, Stain (action, at will).** Touch a creature; it knows every harm it has done to an innocent in the last day. A creature that has done such harm has disadvantage on its next three attack rolls. **Parts.** *Basin:* a creature you cleanse of guilt regains 2d6 hit points. *Lasting Mark:* the stain stays visible to you for an hour. **Maxim, Crowd's Verdict (long rest, 1 minute).** Everyone in 60 feet is affected at once.

name: Ferjukarl
md:
*Ferryman.* **Holder:** Piet Vos (Usher). **Idol:** Charon, "The Ferryman." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** The boatman of the underworld takes the dead across the river for a coin.

**Blueprint, Pay the Coin (action, short rest).** Take up to four creatures across a river, chasm, or barrier of up to 60 feet, instantly and safely, in exchange for a coin from each. **Parts.** *Dark Water:* creatures in the boat cannot be seen from the far shore.

name: Sjónleikr
idol: Georges Méliès, "The Magician of the Screen."
md:
*Spectacle.* **Holder:** Ines Calder (Prop Master). **Idol:** Georges Méliès, "The Magician of the Screen." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A stage magician turned to film and discovered that stopping the camera and starting again could make anything appear or vanish.

**Blueprint, Stop Trick (action, at will).** Create a minor illusion that looks and sounds real from any angle for 10 minutes, and swap one object with another within 30 feet. **Parts.** *Substitution Splice:* a creature you swap appears in the other's place unharmed. *Smoke Cue:* the swap leaves a puff of smoke only you can see.

name: Leikandi
md:
*Player.* **Holder:** Tobi Adeyemi (Stagehand). **Idol:** Thespis, "The First Actor." **Burden** 1, **level** 1.

**Story.** A chorus member stepped out and spoke as if he were someone else, and the theater was born.

**Blueprint, Cue (action, at will).** You can mimic any voice or sound you have heard and throw your voice up to 60 feet.

name: Fjǫtrar
md:
*Fetters.* **Holder:** Orcineus. **Idol:** Snorri Sturluson, "The Edda-Writer" (proposed). **Burden** 6, **level** 17.

**Story.** The gods could not bind the great wolf with any chain of iron, so the dwarves made a ribbon of six impossible things: the sound of a cat's footfall, a woman's beard, a mountain's roots, a bear's sinews, a fish's breath, a bird's spittle. The wolf bit off a hand as the price of letting it be tied.

**Blueprint, The Soft Chain (action, short rest).** Bind a creature within 60 feet in a ribbon that looks like nothing at all. It must pass a Strength save or be held fast, unable to move, attack, or cast, for 1 hour. It repeats the save only once, at dawn. Creatures of 9th level or lower cannot break it. **Parts.** *Cat's Footfall:* the ribbon makes no sound and cannot be sensed. *Woman's Beard:* the bound creature cannot be healed or freed by any ally's magic. *Roots of the Mountain:* the bound creature cannot be teleported. *Bear's Sinew:* its Strength score is treated as 1 while bound. *Breath of Fish:* it does not need to breathe, and cannot suffocate. *Spittle of Bird:* it cannot speak. **Maxim, Gleipnir (long rest, 1 minute).** You may bind up to three creatures at once, or one creature of any level. **Signature Part, A Hand in the Jaws.** While a creature is bound, you know exactly what it wants to do. **Price.** One of your hands is held in the bound creature's jaws; you cannot use it for a day.

name: Hundraðauga
md:
*Hundred-Eyed.* **Holder:** Dagny Arvidsóttir. **Idol:** Argus Panoptes, "The All-Seeing." **Burden** 5, **level** 11.

**Story.** A giant had a hundred eyes, and only some slept at a time. The gods sent a god of dreams with a flute to put all of them to sleep, and still his eyes were set in a peacock's tail.

**Blueprint, Watch (at will).** You see in all directions out to 120 feet, cannot be surprised, and always know the location of every creature you have bound or charged with. **Parts.** *Eyes That Sleep in Turn:* you never need sleep. *Peacock Tail:* eyes you have placed on a location remain there for a day. *Count the Flock:* you know the number of creatures within 120 feet. **Maxim, All Eyes Open (long rest, 1 minute).** You see through walls and illusions and know the intentions of every creature in range. **Signature Part, Only Sleep Can Close Them.** A sleep spell or flute-like sound is the only thing that can blind you. **Price.** You must keep watch on a specific location while the Fable is active, and cannot leave your post.

name: Óendahlekkr
idol: The Smith Who Forged Without End
md:
*Infinity Chain.* **Holder:** Aurelio Vance. **Idol:** The Smith Who Forged Without End. **Burden** 4, **level** 5.

**Story.** A smith forged a chain to bind a storm and never found its last link. Every nation on that layer of Yggdrasil tells it as the chain that has no end. Suggested Idol: The Smith Who Forged Without End.

**Blueprint, Endless Chain (at will).** The bearer lets out up to 120 feet of chain as an attack or a grapple. A creature it hits is restrained (escape DC = the Fable's save DC). The chain cannot be cut by nonmagical means. Only one creature can be restrained at a time. **Blueprint, Bridge of Links (action, twice per long rest).** Lay a chain walkway up to 120 feet long and 5 feet wide between two points you can see. It lasts 1 hour and holds up to 10 creatures. **Parts.** *Unbroken:* Endless Chain can bind creatures it normally could not touch; incorporeal, ethereal and gaseous creatures are restrained as if solid, and a restrained creature cannot teleport or leave the plane while bound. *Second Link:* Endless Chain can hold a second creature within 10 feet of the first. *Long Span:* Bridge of Links can reach 1 mile, and creatures on the bridge cannot be pushed, pulled or knocked off it. **Maxim, No End (long rest, 1 minute).** Redraws Endless Chain. Chains erupt from the air in a 30-foot radius around the bearer. Creatures of the bearer's choice make a Strength save or are restrained, and repeat the save at the end of each of their turns (6th-level effect). **Chant.** "By the Smith Who Forged Without End, I ask that no one leave my sight. Óendahlekkr."

name: Eyra
md:
*The Ear.* **Holder:** Marcus Tullio. **Idol:** Dionysius I, "The Tyrant of Syracuse." **Burden** 4, **level** 9.

**Story.** A tyrant had a cave carved in the shape of an ear, so that every whisper from his prisoners echoed to the one place where he sat listening.

**Blueprint, Listen at the Wall (action, at will).** Choose a building, cell, or chamber within 120 feet. You hear everything said inside it as if you stood beside every speaker. **Parts.** *Curved Stone:* whispers within the area are carried to you even through magical silence. *Sealed Ear:* creatures in the room hear only what you want them to hear. **Maxim, The Tyrant's Ear (long rest, 1 minute).** You can also speak to anyone in the area, and your voice sounds like it comes from within their own head. **Signature Part, All Secrets Echo.** Every secret spoken within the area is added to a list in your memory that you can recall perfectly. **Price.** You cannot listen in on a room that has a living creature in it who has asked you not to.

name: Hárlás
md:
*Hair-Lock.* **Holder:** Reuben Strand. **Idol:** Samson, "The Shorn Judge." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A strongman was betrayed by a woman who cut his hair while he slept, and so lost the strength that came with it.

**Blueprint, Cut the Lock (action, short rest).** Cut a lock of hair from a creature you touch. It must pass a Constitution save or lose its Strength bonus and any magical enhancement for 1 hour. **Parts.** *Keepsake:* the cut lock tracks the creature for a day. *Regrowth:* the creature regains its strength early if you return the lock. **Maxim, Temple Pillars (long rest, 1 minute).** The effect extends to every creature in 30 feet, and a cut lock can be used to bring one down.

name: Hrafnvǫrðr
idol: The Ravens of the Tower, "Keepers of the Crown."
md:
*Raven-Warden.* **Holder:** Edmund Fenwick. **Idol:** The Ravens of the Tower, "Keepers of the Crown." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** An old belief says that if the ravens ever leave the tower, the kingdom will fall.

**Blueprint, Murder of Eyes (action, long rest).** Summon three ravens that scout out to a mile and report what they see. They can peck at a creature to distract it. **Parts.** *Crown's Ravens:* the ravens cannot be killed by anything short of a god's hand. *Tower Rooks:* they can carry notes and objects. **Maxim, The Kingdom Stays (long rest, 1 minute).** The ravens are a swarm of fifty that deal 3d6 piercing damage to anything you name.

name: Steinrúlla
md:
*Stone-Roll.* **Holder:** Ottoline Pryce. **Idol:** Sisyphus, "The Stone-Roller." **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A king who cheated death was condemned to roll a boulder up a hill forever, and it always rolled back.

**Blueprint, Endless Labor (action, short rest).** A creature you touch must pass a Wisdom save or be compelled to repeat a single task over and over for 1 hour, taking no other action. **Parts.** *The Hill:* the task cannot be completed by any means. *Resigned:* the creature is not harmed and does not tire. **Maxim, Hill Without End (long rest, 1 minute).** Up to four creatures are affected at once.

name: Tunna
md:
*The Barrel.* **Holder:** Tomas Brek. **Idol:** Diogenes, "The Dog in the Barrel." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** A philosopher lived in a barrel and told a king standing in his light to step aside.

**Blueprint, Step Out of My Light (action, short rest).** Make a barrel-sized shelter that can hold one creature safely for an hour and blocks all magic and light from outside. **Parts.** *Sun Seeker:* anyone in the barrel has cover against all ranged effects.

name: Lyklavǫrðr
idol: Saint Peter, "The Keeper of the Keys."
md:
*Keeper of Keys.* **Holder:** Cecily Ward. **Idol:** Saint Peter, "The Keeper of the Keys." **Burden** 2, **level** 1.

**Story.** An apostle was given the keys to the gates of heaven and told that what he bound would be bound.

**Blueprint, Bind and Loose (action, at will).** Lock or unlock any ordinary lock with a touch. The lock stays as you set it for an hour. **Parts.** *Ring of Many:* the key can open any lock a person you can name has opened.

name: Tryggr Hundr
md:
*Faithful Hound.* **Holder:** Robert "Bobby" Mackay. **Idol:** Greyfriars Bobby, "The Loyal Dog." **Burden** 1, **level** 1.

**Story.** A dog is said to have sat on his master's grave for fourteen years.

**Blueprint, Keep the Post (at will).** While you stand watch at a single location, you cannot be surprised, and you have advantage on checks to stay awake and to notice approaching creatures.

name: Austrundr
md:
*Wonders of the East.* **Holder:** Beatrix Halloran. **Idol:** Marco Polo, "Il Milione." **Burden** 5, **level** 11.

**Story.** A merchant came back from twenty-four years in the East with tales of cities of gold, paper money, and black stones that burned. His fellow citizens called him a liar and nicknamed his book after the million lies he must have told. On his deathbed he said he had not told half of what he saw.

**Blueprint, Tell the Marvel (action, long rest).** Describe a wonder in no more than three sentences: a bridge, a beast, a feast, a city wall. It becomes real within 120 feet and lasts 1 hour. It can be a creature (challenge 7 or lower) or a structure up to 60 feet on a side. **Parts.** *Not Half:* a second telling adds a feature to the same wonder, once. *Believed Enough:* the more creatures who hear the tale, the sturdier the wonder (+10 temporary hit points per listener). *Paper Money:* a wonder that is a thing of value is usable as currency. **Maxim, A Million (long rest, 1 minute).** You can tell up to three wonders at once, each lasting the whole minute. **Signature Part, Told Only the Half.** Once per long rest, a wonder you describe cannot be dispelled or countered by anything below 9th level. **Price.** The tale must be one you have actually seen or heard from someone who did. Pure invention fails.

name: Eldhús
idol: The Cook Who Fed the Siege
md:
*Fire-House.* **Holder:** Osric Dunmore. **Idol:** The Cook Who Fed the Siege. **Burden** 3, **level** 3.

**Story.** A cook kept a besieged town fed for a winter with whatever the kitchen held, until people said she had brought everything but the kitchen sink. A whole city tells it. Suggested Idol: The Cook Who Fed the Siege.

**Blueprint, Summon the Kitchen (action, twice per short rest).** One appliance appears in an open space within 30 feet and lasts 1 minute. Only one can be out at a time. Each is a Large object with AC 15 and 30 hit points, and gives half cover.
